definitionEn: an electronic machine that stores and processes information
example: Turn off the computer when you finish.

definitionEn: a portable computer you can put on your lap
example: I do homework on a laptop.

definitionEn: a flat computer you control by touching the screen
example: A tablet computer is lighter than a laptop.

definitionEn: a computer that stays on a desk and is not portable
example: The desktop at school is faster than my laptop.

definitionEn: the set of keys you type on
example: Dust under the keyboard makes it sticky.

definitionEn: the small device you move to control the pointer
example: The computer mouse needs new batteries.

definitionEn: a screen you control by touching it
example: The ticket machine has a touchscreen.

definitionEn: a device that plays sound
example: The speaker on this phone is quiet.

definitionEn: a camera on a computer for video calls
example: Cover the webcam when you are not using it.

definitionEn: a device that picks up your voice
example: Mute the microphone in a noisy room.

definitionEn: a small device you plug in to save files
example: Save the presentation on a USB stick.

definitionEn: the part of a computer that stores files permanently
example: The hard drive is almost full.

definitionEn: the part of a computer that holds data while you work
example: This game needs more memory.

definitionEn: the part of a computer that does the calculations
example: A faster processor makes video editing easier.

definitionEn: the main software that runs a computer, such as Windows
example: Which operating system is on the school laptops?

definitionEn: a document, picture or other item stored on a computer
example: Name the file clearly before you send it.

definitionEn: a place on a computer where you keep related files
example: Put homework in the English computer folder.

definitionEn: a small picture on the screen that opens a program
example: Double-click the icon to open the app.

definitionEn: a program you use to look at websites
example: Chrome is a popular browser.

definitionEn: a place on the internet with pages you can visit
example: The school website has the timetable.

definitionEn: one page of a website
example: This webpage takes a long time to load.

definitionEn: text or a button that takes you to another page
example: Click the link in the email.

definitionEn: the address of a website
example: Copy the URL and send it to me.

definitionEn: wireless internet you can use in a place
example: The café Wi-Fi is free but slow.

definitionEn: the box that sends Wi-Fi around a house
example: Restart the router if the internet drops.

definitionEn: a fast internet connection to a home or school
example: We have no broadband in the cottage.

definitionEn: how strong a phone or Wi-Fi connection is
example: There is no signal in the basement.

definitionEn: a system of connected computers
example: Log in to the school network with your username.

definitionEn: storing files on the internet instead of only on your device
example: Save a copy in the cloud in case the laptop breaks.

definitionEn: a second copy of files in case the first is lost
example: Make a backup before you change the computer.

definitionEn: new software that fixes problems or adds features
example: Install the update before you play.

definitionEn: to put a program onto a computer
example: Ask a teacher before you install anything.

definitionEn: to remove a program from a computer
example: Uninstall games you never play.

definitionEn: to switch a computer off and on again
example: Reboot the laptop if the screen freezes.

definitionEn: when a computer stops responding
example: The screen may freeze if too many tabs are open.

definitionEn: when a program stops working suddenly
example: The app may crash if the phone is too old.

definitionEn: a mistake in software that causes problems
example: The game has a bug that deletes saves.

definitionEn: harmful software that can damage files or steal data
example: A computer virus came in that email.

definitionEn: software that finds and stops harmful programs
example: Keep the antivirus up to date.

definitionEn: a person who breaks into computer systems
example: A hacker stole passwords from the company.

definitionEn: to lock a file or device so you need a password
example: Password-protect the folder with photos.

definitionEn: options that control who can see your information
example: Check your privacy settings on social media.

definitionEn: information that identifies you, such as your name or address
example: Do not share personal data with strangers.

definitionEn: a title that tricks you into opening a page
example: That headline is clickbait — do not open it.

definitionEn: stories that look like news but are not true
example: Check another source if you suspect fake news.

definitionEn: a person who advertises products to followers online
example: That influencer is paid to like the drink.

definitionEn: a person who sees your posts on social media
example: She has a thousand followers but few real friends.

definitionEn: a word with # that groups posts on a topic
example: Use the hashtag of the school event.

definitionEn: a small picture used in messages instead of words
example: An emoji is not enough if you are really sorry.

definitionEn: a short written message sent to a phone
example: Send a text message if you will be late.

definitionEn: a phone or computer call where you can see the other person
example: We had a video call with grandma.

definitionEn: an electronic letter sent over the internet
example: Check your email every morning.

definitionEn: a file you send with an email
example: The homework is in the attachment.

definitionEn: unwanted emails, often advertisements
example: Delete spam without opening it.

definitionEn: the folder where new emails arrive
example: There are twenty messages in my inbox.

definitionEn: to look for information on the internet or in files
example: Search for the word in the document.

definitionEn: an important word you type into a search engine
example: Use a better keyword to find the article.

definitionEn: a square pattern a phone camera can read
example: Scan the QR code to open the menu.

definitionEn: a way for devices near you to connect without cables
example: Connect the headphones by bluetooth.

definitionEn: the wire that connects a charger to a device
example: I forgot my charger cable at school.

definitionEn: a battery pack that charges a phone when you travel
example: Take a power bank on the trip.

definitionEn: the socket where you plug in wired headphones
example: This phone has no headphones jack.

definitionEn: how loud the sound is
example: Turn the volume down — I cannot think.

definitionEn: how light or dark a screen is
example: Lower the brightness to save battery.

definitionEn: a picture of what is on your screen
example: Send a screenshot of the error.

definitionEn: to watch or send video over the internet without downloading it all first
example: We stream the match because we have no TV.

definitionEn: a spoken programme you can download or stream
example: I listen to an English podcast on the bus.

definitionEn: a website where a person writes regular posts
example: She writes a travel blog.

definitionEn: a video blog, often on YouTube
example: His vlog about school went viral.

definitionEn: to be shared by a huge number of people very quickly
example: The dance clip will go viral by tonight.

definitionEn: computer systems that can do tasks that usually need human thinking
example: Artificial intelligence can check grammar but it also makes mistakes.

definitionEn: a program that answers questions in a chat window
example: The shop chatbot could not help me.

definitionEn: a small flying machine controlled from the ground
example: A drone filmed the school sports day.

definitionEn: a machine that builds objects from a computer design
example: The 3D printer made a plastic phone stand.

definitionEn: a computer world you see through a headset
example: Virtual reality made me dizzy after ten minutes.

definitionEn: a scientific test you do in a lab
example: Write up the laboratory experiment in your notebook.

definitionEn: an idea you test in an experiment
example: Our hypothesis was that plants need light.

definitionEn: what you measure or observe in a test
example: The results did not match the hypothesis.

definitionEn: an instrument that makes tiny things look larger
example: Look at the onion cells under the microscope.

definitionEn: an instrument that makes distant objects in the sky look closer
example: We used a telescope to see the moon.

definitionEn: an object that attracts iron
example: The magnet picked up the paper clips.

definitionEn: energy that powers lights, machines and devices
example: Never mix water and electricity.

definitionEn: a closed path that electricity can travel around
example: The bulb lights when the circuit is complete.

definitionEn: when substances change into new substances
example: Vinegar and baking soda cause a chemical reaction.

definitionEn: the force that pulls things towards the Earth
example: Gravity keeps us on the ground.

definitionEn: the sun and the planets that go around it
example: Earth is the third planet in the solar system.

definitionEn: a large round object that goes around a star
example: Mars is a planet you can sometimes see at night.

definitionEn: a large spacecraft that stays in orbit and people live in
example: Astronauts work on the space station for months.

definitionEn: a person who travels into space
example: The astronaut described the view of Earth.

definitionEn: careful study to find out new facts
example: Scientists do research before they publish.

definitionEn: an explanation based on evidence, not just a guess
example: The theory of gravity explains falling objects.
